citations.assessment: The household of Yosef the fowler brings the case before Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira. Heilprin summarizes with a singular subject.
Levi visits Yosef’s house, where they serve him the peacock. Rabbi asks why he did not excommunicate them, and Levi appeals to the ruling associated with Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira.
The parallel names Rabbi and explicitly says that Levi did not eat.

holds.reason: The currently checked Shabbat and Chullin text reads Rabbi, consistent with the reported deletion. The exact Maharshal gloss and the pre-deletion witness remain unconfirmed.
